chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Abu Ubaydah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who married a free woman and two slave women in a single contract. He said: 'As for the free woman, her marriage is valid, and if he specified a dowry for her, it is hers. As for the two slave women, their marriage in a contract with the free woman is invalid, and he is separated from them and they are separated from him.'
Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And if a man marries off his slave woman to his slave man, the dowry is upon him from his own wealth.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying a free woman and two slave women in one contract?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the structural validity of mixed-status marriages, distinguishing between the independent validity of the free woman's contract and the invalidity of the slave women's contracts when bundled with her. The accompanying note from Shaykh al-Tusi highlights the economic distinction in dowry liability, emphasizing that the master bears the cost when marrying his own slave to his slave, reflecting the patriarchal legal framework of the time. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic principle that the status of the bride significantly impacts the contract's integrity and financial obligations.
